brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface (a centre hex base with six surrounding hex bases)
requirements.evidence: Seven Hex base · Full pieces at level 0: axial (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1), forming a flower of seven cells.
Seven Cover · Full pieces on the top face of every cell (cover:-1,0 / -1,1 / 0,-1 / 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,-1 / 1,0), plus 21 cover snaps.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: 18 edge caps (9 male, 9 female in BOM) placed on the 18 open outer edges of the six outer cells (3 per outer cell); the centre cell has no open outer edge. check_build reports no rule issues and meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Structure held together (not in brief, added to clear LOOSE_BODY warning)
requirements.evidence: Joint bolts (M6, 12 walls bolted) added so the six-piece body no longer can slide apart; check_build is clean. Bolts are to be hand-tightened to about 2 N.m per the BOM note.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell flower of Hex base · Full pieces, each cell covered on top, with 18 edge caps closing all open outside edges. Joint bolts were added to lock the pieces together; check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear. Print estimate about 2.7 kg PETG-class filament and 4010 minutes, per the BOM.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
